top_story.headline: House bill would bar candidates from betting on their own elections
top_story.dek: Rep. Donald Davis introduced a measure during a brief pro forma House session on Monday.
paragraphs: Rep. Donald Davis (D-NC) introduced H.R. 10732, which would amend title 52 of the United States Code to prohibit candidates for federal office from trading in contracts on the outcome of their own elections. It was referred to the Committee on House Administration.

The Congressional Record lists no cosponsors for the bill, and it gives only the bill's title, so details such as penalties or which markets it covers are not confirmed here. It was one of 30 House bills introduced Monday, during a session where neither chamber held a vote.

sections.headline: Pro forma sessions only; 41 House measures introduced
paragraphs: The Senate met in a pro forma session at 4:00 p.m., lasting under a minute, and adjourned until 1:30 p.m. Tuesday. The House met at 4:30 p.m. and adjourned at 4:33 p.m.; there were no roll call votes and no quorum calls. Both chambers are scheduled for pro forma sessions again Tuesday. (Daily Digest)

The House recorded 30 bills (H.R. 10721-10750) and 11 resolutions (H.Res. 1606-1616). Besides Davis's election-betting bill, notable introductions include H.R. 10740, a Ukraine temporary protected status bill with more than 40 bipartisan cosponsors, and five Medicare and Medicaid bills from Rep. Sharice Davids. Most of the 11 resolutions are commemorative designations. The House also filed a committee report on H.R. 2283, a Veterans Affairs mental health grant pilot program (H. Rept. 119-839). Every measure is listed below.

items: H.R. 10721, sponsored by Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ) — would strengthen bonding and timely cleanup requirements for land and water disturbed by federal and Indian oil and gas production (Mineral Leasing Act). Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.
H.R. 10722, sponsored by Rep. Troy Carter (D-LA) — would expand behavioral health workforce training programs under the Public Health Service Act. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10723, sponsored by Rep. Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ) — would create a bilateral rapid response protocol with Mexico for serious crimes committed against United States citizens there. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.
H.R. 10724, sponsored by Rep. J. Luis Correa (D-CA) — would clarify the bankruptcy rules on exceptions to discharge of an individual debtor's debts. Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10725, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS) — would make reforms to Medicare supplemental (Medigap) health insurance policies. Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means and, additionally, the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10726, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS) — would let individuals with Alzheimer's disease buy in to Medicare. Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means and, additionally, the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10727, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS) — would give priority to expanding service applications from certain entities under the Public Health Service Act. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10728, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS) — would exempt certain maternity, labor and delivery services from limits on Medicaid state-directed payments. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10729, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS) — would adjust the limits on Medicaid state-directed payments and repeal certain provider tax provisions in Public Law 119-21. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10730, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS) — would modify the premium tax credit under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and, additionally, the Committee on Ways and Means.
H.R. 10731, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS) — would adjust the Medicare cost pass-through for certified registered nurse anesthetists. Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10732, sponsored by Rep. Donald Davis (D-NC) — would amend title 52 of the United States Code to bar candidates for federal office from trading in contracts on the outcome of their own elections. Referred to the Committee on House Administration.
H.R. 10733, sponsored by Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-PA) — would establish a Science Advisory Board at the Department of Justice. Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10734, sponsored by Rep. Debbie Dingell (D-MI) — would set standards of liability for harassment on the basis of sex under title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.

H.R. 10735, sponsored by Rep. Gabe Evans (R-CO) — would require certain types of cattle to be included in a livestock pilot program under the Federal Crop Insurance Act. Referred to the Committee on Agriculture.

H.R. 10736, sponsored by Rep. Brad Finstad (R-MN) — would prohibit federal acquisitions of computers or printers involving entities owned or controlled by China. Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.R. 10737, sponsored by Rep. Scott Franklin (R-FL) — would promote transparency in science through changes to the Environmental Research, Development, and Demonstration Authorization Act of 1978; it has 13 listed cosponsors. Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.

H.R. 10738, sponsored by Rep. James Gallagher (R-CA) — would require consideration of discounted electric rates for consumers in counties that host certain power generation facilities. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10739, sponsored by Rep. Michael Guest (R-MS) — would encourage people to enter the forensic pathology workforce. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and, additionally, the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10740, sponsored by Rep. William Keating (D-MA) — would designate Ukraine for temporary protected status so certain Ukrainian nationals keep continued eligibility; it lists more than 40 cosponsors from both parties. Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
H.R. 10741, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) — would enhance the supply of child care. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and four other committees.

H.R. 10742, sponsored by Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) — would direct the Secretary of Defense to report on lessons the United States Armed Forces can learn from defense innovations in the Russia-Ukraine War. Referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10743, sponsored by Rep. Susie Lee (D-NV) — would stop Nonprofit Security Grant Program awards from being treated as reimbursements for costs already incurred. Referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and, additionally, the Committee on Homeland Security.

H.R. 10744, sponsored by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) — would exempt small-scale red meat producers and processors from parts of the Federal Meat Inspection Act. Referred to the Committee on Agriculture.

H.R. 10745, sponsored by Rep. Mary Miller (R-IL) — would prevent the removal of children from their homes over what the bill calls "sex-rejecting interventions." Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and two other committees.

H.R. 10746, sponsored by Rep. Ayanna Pressley (D-MA) — would require a reduction of financial sector emissions to protect financial stability, amending the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 and the Financial Stability Act of 2010. Referred to the Committee on Financial Services.

H.R. 10747, sponsored by Rep. Raul Ruiz (D-CA) — would ensure appropriate geographic adjustments to Medicare Advantage benchmarks in Puerto Rico. Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means and, additionally, the Committee on Energy and Commerce.
H.R. 10748, sponsored by Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY) — would require a report on security cooperation with Western Balkan countries. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.R. 10749, sponsored by Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL) — would authorize emergency assistance for high-value crop losses under the Agricultural Act of 2014. Referred to the Committee on Agriculture.

H.R. 10750, sponsored by Rep. George Whitesides (D-CA) — would direct the Secretary of the Air Force to start a pilot program for in-space demonstrations of advanced nuclear fission and fusion propulsion. Referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
H.Res. 1606, sponsored by Rep. Becca Balint (D-VT) — supports designating October 24-31, 2026, as "Bat Week." Referred to the Committee on Agriculture.
H.Res. 1607, sponsored by Rep. Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR) — supports designating September 2026 as "National Workforce Development Month." Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.
H.Res. 1608, sponsored by Rep. Judy Chu (D-CA) — supports designating October 5, 2026, as "National Beyond the Milky Way Day." Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.

H.Res. 1609, sponsored by Rep. Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ) — honors the life and service of Marine Corps veteran Nicholas Douglas Quets, offers condolences to his family and condemns cartel violence. Referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.Res. 1610, sponsored by Rep. Yvette Clarke (D-NY) — supports recognizing October 2026 as "World Menopause Awareness Month." Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and two other committees.
H.Res. 1611, sponsored by Rep. Jim Costa (D-CA) — supports designating October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day." Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.Res. 1612, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) — honors Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073 and condemns the attempted terrorist attack on that flight. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.
H.Res. 1613, sponsored by Rep. Young Kim (R-CA) — supports recognizing October 5 as "National Peroxisomal Disorder Awareness Day." Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.Res. 1614, sponsored by Rep. Glenn Thompson (R-PA) — supports designating October 4-10, 2026, as "National 4-H Week." Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and, additionally, the Committee on Agriculture.
H.Res. 1615, sponsored by Rep. Norma Torres (D-CA) — supports designating October 2, 2026, as "Manufacturing Day." Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.Res. 1616, sponsored by Rep. David Valadao (R-CA) — recognizes the importance of biodiversity conservation and welcomes Armenia as host of the Seventeenth Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.
